subject.title: ACP: support non-thread persistent affinity for cron and orchestrator sessions

question: Should OpenClaw add a separate ACP persistent-affinity contract for cron/hook/orchestrator callers, or should this wait for the broader non-thread persistent-session design?
rationale: The missing code path is clear, but the permanent API controls session ownership, resume authority, lifecycle cleanup, and security scope; automation should not choose those boundaries.

options.title: Define narrow ACP affinity
options.body: Add a dedicated `affinityKey`/persistent ACP path limited to cron, hook, or orchestrator requesters with explicit owner, backend, cwd, lifecycle, and failure-preservation rules.

options.title: Fold into broader session decoupling
options.body: Keep this issue open as a dependent slice of the broader non-thread `mode="session"` contract so one product shape covers native and ACP persistence.

options.title: Defer cron/hook persistence
options.body: Leave current `mode="run"` and thread-bound `mode="session"` behavior unchanged until scheduled ACP and hub delegation semantics settle.

recommendation.title: Define narrow ACP affinity
recommendation.body: Add a dedicated `affinityKey`/persistent ACP path limited to cron, hook, or orchestrator requesters with explicit owner, backend, cwd, lifecycle, and failure-preservation rules.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent ACP spawn refactor and current file ownership make this the best available routing candidate for the product/security decision.
